correctness.rationale: The three normalized interval measures have mutually disjoint masses, and their two-dimensional span W_t=J ker(1,1,t) is the annihilator of exactly the two asserted independent mean constraints. Any projection on the real weighted zero-sum plane V_t in l1^3 is R=I-u(1,1,t), with a.u=1. For r=1+t/(1+t+t²), the fixed-sign column evaluations L1=1-u1+u2+u3, L2=1+u1-u2+u3, L3=1+t(u1+u2-u3) and b=t(1+t)/2>0 obey the identity b(L1+L2)+L3=(2b+1)r. Thus max column norm>=r; u*=((1+t)/(2s),(1+t)/(2s),t/s), s=1+t+t², has all three exact norms r. Equality in the positive certificate forces all L_i=r and uniquely u*. Isometric J into signed measures and contractive interval-mass B yield lambda(W_t,M[0,1])=r. Kania–Lewicki 2026 Theorem 3.1 (using local reflexivity) yields lambda(Y_t,C[0,1])=1+r. If a norm-minimizing P existed, its complementary adjoint would be weak-star continuous with Q delta_s=J g(s), where g:[0,1]->V_t is continuous and ||g(s)||_1<=r. Restriction to the three-block source forces the interval averages g over I1 and I2 to equal the unique first two optimum columns; they norm at r against signs (+,-,-) and (-,+,-). Their scalar norming functions must equal r on the respective closed intervals. At the shared boundary both signs norm g, forcing g=(0,0,-r), impossible since (1,1,t).g=-tr!=0 for t>0. Finally derivative of t/(1+t+t²) is (1-t²)/(1+t+t²)²>0 on (0,1), giving precisely (2,7/3]. Independently verified the rational/ symbolic identities, unique optimum and signed-face compatibility; 16,250 rational checks are corroboration, not a proof of the analytical argument.

value.rationale: The family gives a natural explicit codimension-two subspace defined by adjacent interval means, resolving the specific n=2 fixed-codimension nonattainment interval posed in Kania–Lewicki 2026 Question 6.2, including the sharp nonattained endpoint 7/3. It separates the finite-dimensional extremal plane norm from the topological obstruction to realizing a minimizer by continuous dual coefficients, yielding a mathematically reusable saturated-face criterion; this is substantially more than a routine rational check or a tiny numerical improvement. The full interval and endpoint are natural and not mechanically implied by the prior value of the absolute planar constant.
